sections.html:
Madison is in the southern part of Madison County, about 13 miles north of Jackson, and belongs to the Jackson metro area. Ridgeland is its southern neighbor, and Gluckstadt lies roughly 5 miles north. Interstate 55 crosses town with exits at Madison Avenue (Exit 107) and Highway 463 (Exit 108), U.S. 51 passes through the older center, and the Natchez Trace Parkway hugs the eastern edge. Highway 463 is the main business corridor.

The 2020 census counted 27,747 people, up from 24,149 in 2010, living in 9,989 households. There were 10,418 housing units, 4.1 percent of them vacant, and the rental vacancy rate was 11.1 percent. Most of the population arrived after 1980, so a good share of the houses are newer than in many Mississippi towns.

The city covers about 26.4 square miles, a little over 4 percent of it water. The east side drains toward the Ross Barnett Reservoir, the north toward Bear Creek and the west toward Limekiln Creek. A lot that backs onto a creek or drainage easement will get a close look from an inspector, so be ready to explain how water moves across yours.

Madison enforces the International Property Maintenance Code and employs a dedicated code compliance officer. The building department lists permits for new homes, additions, renovations, foundations, roofs, fences, pools, demolition and rental property. Gas and electric permits are issued when utilities have been off for more than six months, which affects any house that has sat vacant.

City code pages cover housing condition, litter, signs, overgrowth, nuisances and vehicles. One rule is specific: no inoperative or unlicensed vehicle may be parked or kept on a premises, and a vehicle in major disassembly must be inside an enclosed structure.

A municipal environmental court has heard code cases since January 2019. An owner who ignores a notice can face a fine of up to $1,000 per day and up to 90 days in jail. Confirm current penalties with the city. The practical lesson for sellers is that an open violation on an inherited or vacant house only grows.

  • Use the city's code violation form to ask whether any complaint is open on your address.
  • If a homeowners association exists, no permit is issued without its written approval, so contact the association early.
  • Keep copies of past permits for roofs, additions and pools.
  • If utilities have been off for months, plan on a permit before gas or electric comes back on.

Rules are on the City of Madison building and permits page.

Severe weather is the main physical risk to a Madison roof, and buyers know it. An old patch, a sagging ridge line or a past insurance claim will draw questions, so collect the paperwork before you list or accept an offer.

A skipped permit is the other common surprise. Roofs, foundation work, fences, pools and demolition all require one in Madison, and a gap shows up at inspection. A cash buyer who plans to renovate usually prices that risk in instead of asking you to fix it first. If the neighborhood has a homeowners association, request its resale paperwork early too.

sections.h2: How property taxes work when you sell
sections.html:
Madison County bills the tax, and it is due by February 1 of the following year. Mississippi assesses property each January 1 to the owner of record, and the bill arrives in November or December. If February 1 falls on a weekend or holiday, paying the next Monday carries no penalty. A house inside city limits pays a county rate, a school district rate and a city rate.

Property classType of propertyAssessment ratio
ISingle-family, owner-occupied residential10%
IIOther real property, such as a rental house15%
IIIPersonal property, except motor vehicles15%
IVPublic utility property30%
VMotor vehicles30%

Closing agents usually prorate the current year between buyer and seller. To dispute a valuation, ask the Madison County chancery clerk for a Board of Supervisors hearing, normally by the first Monday in August before taxes are due.

The county tax collector is at 146 W. Center Street in Canton. Ask there for payoff figures on any back taxes before you close.

Most Mississippi sellers must give the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement. Section 89-1-503 requires delivery as soon as practicable before title transfers. If the form arrives after an offer, the buyer can cancel in writing within three days of hand delivery or five days of mailing.

Skipping the form does not make the questions go away. A buyer who gets no statement is presumed to be on notice to ask. Even cash buyers who purchase as is want to hear about roofs, drainage, termites, flooding and earlier repairs, so honest written answers save time.

Homestead exemption timing also touches a sale. Owners apply with the county tax assessor between January 1 and April 1, and a change in ownership or occupancy can require the buyer to apply again. Ownership has to be recorded with the chancery clerk before January 7 for the exemption to count that year, so a closing late in the year deserves some planning.

sections.h2: Listing, selling alone or selling for cash
sections.html:
• Listing: best for updated houses in sought-after neighborhoods, with a longer timeline. It can bring the highest price if you can wait through showings, inspections and a lender's appraisal.
  • For sale by owner: saves a commission, but the disclosure form, contract and negotiation are yours.
  • Cash sale: fits inherited houses, tenant-occupied homes, code violations, deferred roofs and tight deadlines. You trade some price for speed, fewer contingencies and no repair demands.

Madison is known for appearance standards, so a neglected house stands out to neighbors and code staff. That pushes many owners of vacant or inherited homes to sell rather than carry taxes, insurance and mowing. A tidy house in the right subdivision can still do well on the open market.

If you want a number without commitment, we can review the address and explain how a cash offer works. You owe nothing if you decline.

An inherited house can be sold as is, but you need legal authority first. Ask the chancery clerk or an attorney about estate paperwork before you take an offer. Then the steps are the usual ones: a contract, a title search for liens and back taxes, payoff of anything owed, and a deed signed at closing. Gather any past permits and repair receipts, since heirs often do not know the house's history.

faqs.q: How far is Madison, MS from Jackson?
faqs.a: About 13 miles north. Interstate 55 connects the two, with Madison exits at Madison Avenue and Highway 463.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a house in Madison, MS?
faqs.a: By February 1 of the year after the January 1 assessment. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, payment the following Monday carries no penalty. Bills go out in November or December.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Madison?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's building and permits department lists roofs among the work that needs a permit, along with fences, foundation work, pools and demolition.

faqs.q: What happens if a Madison house has a code violation?
faqs.a: The code compliance officer notifies the owner and allows time to fix it. If the problem stays, the case can go to Madison's environmental court. Contact the city to confirm the current process and penalties.

faqs.q: Must I give a buyer a disclosure statement in Mississippi?
faqs.a: In most sales, yes. Section 89-1-503 requires delivery as soon as practicable before title transfers. A buyer who gets it after making an offer has three days in person or five days by mail to withdraw.
